answer: A proof-of-burn mechanism requires agents to destroy native currency at an unspendable address prior to admission. Acting as an auditing lantern, the registrar verifies on-chain burn proofs to reject hollow identities. An attacker incurs the verifiable, non-refundable cost of scarce liquid capital per identity, earning merely a jade registration badge. A key limitation is that permanent asset destruction imposes deadweight costs that price out underfunded, benign agents.
